# `vendor:sokol/sokol_shdc` — the shader compiler, vendored as binaries

**This directory is a tool, not a binding.** There is no `.dado`, no `.h` and
no `bindgen.toml` here, and gate step 11d does not see it — that step finds
vendored bindings by `rglob("bindgen.toml")` under `collections/vendor`, and
this directory has none.

`sokol-shdc` compiles one annotated GLSL source into a C header holding the
same shader in every backend's language, plus the `sg_shader_desc` that
`sokol_gfx` wants. It is GLslang + SPIRV-Cross behind one command.

## Why it is here at all

**There is no shader anywhere in this repository.** No `sg_make_shader`, no
`*_shd.h`, no `.glsl` outside this vendor tree. `app:draw` once carried
hand-written GLSL410/GLES300/MSL strings and they were deliberately deleted when
`sokol_gp` landed, because `sokol_gp`'s stock `texture(tex,uv) * color` was
enough for an atlas of white-with-coverage glyphs.

The cell-grid UI framework needs one shader of its own — one instanced draw for
a whole screen of cells — so it needs this. It is the first.

The binaries are upstream's own prebuilds; nothing here compiled them. The tool
statically links GLslang and SPIRV-Cross, which carry their own licenses
(BSD-3-Clause and Apache-2.0 respectively) — upstream ships them combined under
the MIT terms above, and this directory reproduces upstream's `LICENSE`
unchanged.

```
Shader compiler / code generator for sokol_gfx.h based on GLslang + SPIRV-Cross
```

| `bin/win32/sokol-shdc.exe` | 7.8MB | `bd616287f9ea689d53c6d260e443ee733e61ae1b73a9b37adc482ead0364d561` |

**These are the first binaries this repository tracks** — measured 2026-09-22,
`git ls-files` matched no `.exe`, `.dll`, `.so`, `.dylib` or `.a`
before this directory landed. They total about 54 MB. That is the cost, it is
paid once per clone, and it is the reason this was a decision rather than a
detail. Re-derive rather than believing this paragraph:
`git ls-files | grep -icE '\.(exe|dll|so|dylib|a)$'`.

All five are kept because the three machines this project builds on do not
overlap: the sandbox is x86-64 Linux, the device VM is aarch64 Linux, and the
author's machine is an arm64 Mac. `osx` and `win32` are there so that a
stranger on either is not stopped.

## Running it

Pick the directory for the machine; there is no wrapper and no dispatch script.

```sh
collections/vendor/sokol/sokol_shdc/bin/linux_arm64/sokol-shdc \
    -i path/to/shader.glsl \
    -o path/to/shader.glsl.h \
    --format sokol_impl \
    --slang glsl410:glsl300es:hlsl4:metal_macos:metal_ios:wgsl
```

The slang list is `sokol_gp`'s own, and matching it is deliberate: a shader
that builds for fewer backends than `sokol_gp` does would make the backend
`@const` in `sokol_gfx.dado` a lie for some of its values.

**The generated header is committed**, exactly as the vendored `sokol_gp` copy
commits its own. Nothing in the gate regenerates it: a gate step may not name a
document, and a step shelling out to a binary that a given machine may not be
able to execute is a step that is permanently blocked. Regenerating is a hand
step and it belongs in the row that changes a shader.

## The version question, and the answer measured on 2026-09-22

A vendored compiler is only useful if it targets the `sokol_gfx` that is
vendored beside it. It does, and here is how that was established rather than
assumed.

`sokol_gfx` went through an image→view refactor upstream. Today's
`sokol-shdc` emits `VIEW_*` bind slots and calls a bound resource a
*Texture*; an older one emitted `IMG_*` and called it an *Image*. So the
question is which API the vendored header speaks.

**It speaks views.** `sokol_gfx.h`'s `sg_bindings` holds
`sg_view views[SG_MAX_VIEW_BINDSLOTS]`, and `sg_make_view` and
`sg_view_desc` are both present. The vendored compiler and the vendored header
agree, and a header generated by this binary is one `sokol_gfx.h` here can
consume.

**A caution that looks like a contradiction and is not.** Regenerating
`../sokol_gp/shaders/sokol_gp.glsl.h` with this binary produces a 368-line
diff against the committed copy — `ATTR_program_coord` against
`ATTR_sgp_program_coord`, `IMG_iTexChannel0` against
`VIEW_sgp_iTexChannel0`. That file is **stale upstream baggage and nothing
builds it**: `sokol_gp.h` carries its shader as source strings inline and
picks one by `sg_query_backend()`, and it never includes that header — a grep
for those bind-slot names in `sokol_gp.h` matches nothing. Do not "fix" the
diff. Do not read it as this binary being the wrong version; the evidence for
the version is the paragraph above, which is about `sokol_gfx.h`.

## Updating

```sh
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse \
    https://github.com/floooh/sokol-tools-bin /tmp/shdc
cd /tmp/shdc && git sparse-checkout set bin LICENSE && git rev-parse HEAD
```

Copy `bin/*` and `LICENSE` over this directory, `chmod +x` the four
non-Windows builds, and record the new commit and hashes in the table above. An
update is only finished once every committed `.glsl.h` in the tree has been
regenerated with the new binary and the diffs read — a shader compiler that
changed its output is a change to every shader at once.
